<a id="aln-01"></a>
## ALN-01 - Align related content to a shared edge

Line up text, icons and controls along common axes so the component looks organised; misjudged alignment looks messy.

- **Source:** PDF 17 (printed 16)
- **Applies when:** Cards and components that mix an icon, a title, body text and a button.

**What the PDF states** (paraphrased):
- Alignment lines up text, images and components along lines or axes for a polished, organised look; poor alignment looks messy and is harder to use.
- Bad alignment can come from misjudgement, e.g. an icon placed beside the body so title and body start at different x positions.

**Mistake:** Title starts at the card edge while the body and button are indented to the right of an icon.  
**Effect:** Multiple ragged left edges; the card reads as disorganised.

**Correction:** Put the icon inline with the title in a header row, and align body text and the button to the same left content edge.  
**Why it works:** One strong left edge creates order and an easy reading start point.

**Observable checks:**
- Within a component, count distinct left x-positions used by text blocks and buttons; more than needed signals misalignment.
- Is any block indented without a structural reason?

**Exceptions / limits supported by the source:**
- None stated by the source.

**Related:** [ALN-02](05-alignment.md#aln-02), [ALN-04](05-alignment.md#aln-04)

<a id="aln-02"></a>
## ALN-02 - Align repeated items on common lines

Repeated items such as nav pills must share widths and icon/label positions; forgetting to align is a common cause of messy UIs.

- **Source:** PDF 18 (printed 17)
- **Applies when:** Navigation lists, menus, tabs, list rows.

**What the PDF states** (paraphrased):
- Bad alignment can also come simply from forgetting to align; in the corrected nav list, items share the same width and icons and labels share common left lines.

**Mistake:** List items with differing widths and icon/label offsets.  
**Effect:** Jagged, untidy list that is slower to scan.

**Correction:** Give repeated items identical widths and place icons and labels on shared vertical lines.  
**Why it works:** Shared lines let the eye run straight down the list.

**Observable checks:**
- Do the icons in a repeated list share the same x? Do the labels? Do the item backgrounds share the same width?

**Exceptions / limits supported by the source:**
- None stated by the source.

**Related:** [ALN-04](05-alignment.md#aln-04), [CNS-05](11-consistency.md#cns-05)

<a id="aln-03"></a>
## ALN-03 - Choose alignment by content type

Left-align body text and lists; right-align numbers you compare (and RTL text); centre only short titles or CTAs.

- **Source:** PDF 18 (printed 17), 94 (printed 93), 97 (printed 96)
- **Applies when:** Any text block, table or button group.

**What the PDF states** (paraphrased):
- Left alignment is the go-to for most text (clean edge for paragraphs and lists).
- Right alignment suits numbers such as prices or table data to compare, and right-to-left languages such as Arabic.
- Centre alignment suits titles or CTA buttons; avoid it for longer text because each line starts at a different place.
- Longer paragraphs are best left-aligned for a consistent starting point in left-to-right reading; centre/right are for special cases (titles, short attention-grabbing text, decorative/artistic elements).

**Mistake:** Centre-aligned multi-line paragraphs (e.g. an article card with centred title and body).  
**Effect:** The eye must hunt for each line start, reducing readability.

**Correction:** Left-align paragraphs and lists; reserve centring for short headings or CTAs; right-align comparable numeric columns.  
**Why it works:** A consistent start edge supports natural LTR reading.

**Observable checks:**
- Is any text block of more than two or three lines centre- or right-aligned (in an LTR locale)?
- Are numeric table columns right-aligned so digits line up?

**Exceptions / limits supported by the source:**
- Right alignment is appropriate for RTL languages.
- Centre/right can work for decorative or artistic elements and short text.

**Related:** [TYP-04](15-typography.md#typ-04), [ALN-05](05-alignment.md#aln-05)

<a id="aln-04"></a>
## ALN-04 - Use grids and auto-layout to enforce alignment

A grid system and auto-layout keep elements exactly where they belong and remove manual nudging.

- **Source:** PDF 19 (printed 18), 20 (printed 19)
- **Applies when:** Page layouts (grids) and components (auto-layout / flex / stack spacing).

**What the PDF states** (paraphrased):
- A grid system eases alignment and keeps things consistent (figure shows a Figma layout grid).
- Auto-layout places elements exactly where they should be without manual adjustment (figure shows a vertical stack with fixed spacing and padding).

**Mistake:** Hand-positioned elements with ad-hoc offsets.  
**Effect:** Drift and inconsistency between similar elements.

**Correction:** Lay out pages on a column grid; build components with auto-layout (in code: flex/grid with gap and padding tokens).  
**Why it works:** Systems produce alignment by construction.

**Observable checks:**
- In code: are positions set through layout primitives (flex/grid, gap) rather than absolute offsets or one-off margins?

**Exceptions / limits supported by the source:**
- None stated by the source.

**Interpretation (ours, not stated by the PDF):**
- Figure values (3 columns, margin 79, gutter 70; spacing 24, padding 32) are illustrative Figma settings, not recommendations.

**Related:** [WS-03](08-whitespace.md#ws-03), [ALN-01](05-alignment.md#aln-01)

<a id="aln-05"></a>
## ALN-05 - Stick to one alignment strategy across similar elements

Pick an alignment approach for a component type and use it consistently instead of mixing left and centre.

- **Source:** PDF 20 (printed 19)
- **Applies when:** Product cards, tiles and any repeated component.

**What the PDF states** (paraphrased):
- Choose an alignment strategy and stick with it across similar elements; the incorrect card mixes left and centre ('Alignment: Left & Center'), the correct one is all left.

**Mistake:** Some lines centred (rating, author) while others (title, price) are left-aligned in the same card.  
**Effect:** Inconsistent, unpolished appearance.

**Correction:** Use a single alignment (left in the source example) for all content in the card.  
**Why it works:** Consistency makes components predictable and tidy.

**Observable checks:**
- Within one card type, do all text elements use the same alignment?

**Exceptions / limits supported by the source:**
- None stated by the source.

**Related:** [ALN-03](05-alignment.md#aln-03), [CNS-01](11-consistency.md#cns-01)
